18.3 Ethers

Ethers are a class of organic compounds in which the oxygen atom is linked to two alkyl groups or two aryl groups or one alkyl and one aryl group. Thus the functional group of ethers is C – O – C. They can be represented by the general formula R – O –R. Ethers are described as symmetrical or unsymmetrical depending on whether the two groups bonded to oxygen are the same or different. Unsymmetrical ethers are also called mixed ethers. Diethyl ether is a symmetrical ether; ethyl methyl ether is an unsymmetrical ether (R – O – R′). Examples of ethers are:

18.3.1 Nomenclature

a. Common System

The two alkyl or aryl groups that are attached to the oxygen atom are named in alphabetical order and the word ether is added. When both alkyl groups are the same, the prefix di- precedes the name of the alkyl group.

Examples

b. IUPAC System

Ethers are named in IUPAC nomenclature, as alkoxy derivatives of alkanes. The larger alkyl group is taken for parent name and the smaller alkyl group along with oxygen atom is named as alkoxy before the parent name.

Examples

18.3.2 Physical Properties

Dimethyl ether and ethyl methyl ether are gases at RTP, while others are colourless volatile liquids with pleasant odours.

Ethers are highly inflammable.

They have much lower boiling points than those of alcohols of comparable molecular weights due to absence of hydrogen bonding (Figure 18.3).

Low molecular weight ethers show some solubility in water as they can form hydrogen bonding with water (Figure 18.3). Ethers are readily soluble in organic solvents.

18.3 Ethers

Ethers are a class of organic compounds in which the oxygen atom is linked to two alkyl groups or two aryl groups or one alkyl and one aryl group. Thus the functional group of ethers is C – O – C. They can be represented by the general formula R – O –R. Ethers are described as symmetrical or unsymmetrical depending on whether the two groups bonded to oxygen are the same or different. Unsymmetrical ethers are also called mixed ethers. Diethyl ether is a symmetrical ether; ethyl methyl ether is an unsymmetrical ether (R – O – R′). Examples of ethers are:

18.3.1 Nomenclature

a. Common System

The two alkyl or aryl groups that are attached to the oxygen atom are named in alphabetical order and the word ether is added. When both alkyl groups are the same, the prefix di- precedes the name of the alkyl group.

Examples

b. IUPAC System

Ethers are named in IUPAC nomenclature, as alkoxy derivatives of alkanes. The larger alkyl group is taken for parent name and the smaller alkyl group along with oxygen atom is named as alkoxy before the parent name.

Examples

18.3.2 Physical Properties

Dimethyl ether and ethyl methyl ether are gases at RTP, while others are colourless volatile liquids with pleasant odours.

Ethers are highly inflammable.

They have much lower boiling points than those of alcohols of comparable molecular weights due to absence of hydrogen bonding (Figure 18.3).

Low molecular weight ethers show some solubility in water as they can form hydrogen bonding with water (Figure 18.3). Ethers are readily soluble in organic solvents.
